# Global electric vehicle market monitor for light-duty vehicles in key markets, H1 2026

October 27, 2026 | By: Ilma Fadhil, Dale Hall, and Xingyi Li 

This edition of the Global Market Monitor for Light-duty Vehicles analyzes electric vehicle (EV) trends from the first half of 2026 (H1 2026). It covers sales across the world’s four largest auto markets—China, Europe, the United States, and India—and key emerging markets. 

#### The global market

Globally, over 9.4 million electric vehicles were sold in the first half of 2026, accounting for almost one quarter of all light-duty vehicles (LDVs) sold.

##### 🇨🇳 China

- In H1 2026, EVs comprised over half (51%) of all LDV sales in the country.
- BEVs made up 68% of total EV sales, up from 64% in 2025.

##### 🇪🇺 Europe

- In H1 2026, 31% of all new LDVs sold were EVs, an increase from 27% in 2025.
- BEVs remained the most popular powertrain, accounting for 69% of total EV sales, slightly higher than 2025 and 2024.
- All major manufacturers had a higher BEV sales share than plug-in hybrid electric vehicle (PHEV) sales share, except for Jaguar Land Rover.

##### 🇮🇳 India

- In H1 2026, approximately 146,000 EVs were sold, representing 5% of the country’s new LDV sales, an increase of 1 percentage point from 2025.
- Mahindra and Tata Motors each reached an 8% EV sales share and collectively accounted for over half of all EV sales in the country.
- International manufacturers with substantial LDV market shares registered very low EV sales: Toyota, Hyundai, Kia, Suzuki, and VW Group each had EV sales shares between 0.3% and 0.8%.

##### 🇺🇸 United States

- In H1 2026, approximately 7% of new LDVs sold in the United States were electric, a 2 percentage-point drop from 2025.
- Many legacy manufacturers saw declines in both EV sales volume and EV share of total LDVs sold, reflecting a shift of near-term strategies toward broader powertrain mixes.

#### Emerging markets continue to race ahead 

Electric vehicle sales in the 11 emerging markets profiled in this monitor were 3 percentage points higher in the first half of 2026 than the previous year. 

Vietnam again recorded the highest EV sales share among the selected emerging markets, at 44%, up from 37% in 2025. This once again surpassed the sales share of Europe, the United States, and India. In Latin America, Colombia nearly doubled its EV sales share, from 11% in 2025 to 19% in H1 2026. 

BEVs accounted for nearly all EVs sold in Vietnam and over 90% of sales in Thailand, Türkiye, and Indonesia. Conversely, PHEVs made up a higher share of EVs sold Mexico and South Africa. 

### Philippines 🇵🇭

The fourth largest vehicle market in Southeast Asia is accelerating its EV uptake.

The Philippines is the fourth largest vehicle market in Southeast Asia and one of the fastest growing. Light-duty EV sales have surged from negligible levels (219 units in 2021) to approximately 30,715 units in H1 2026. The market began to accelerate from 2022 onward, driven by zero-tariff and excise tax incentives, as well as the introduction of more affordable BEV and PHEV models from Chinese manufacturers entering the market.

BYD captured the majority of EV sales, accounting for 68% of sales in H1 2026, followed by Tesla (11%) and VinFast (9%). Other Chinese manufacturers, such as Geely (5%) and Chery (4%), continued to gain market share.

By contrast, legacy manufacturers such as Toyota, Hyundai, and Mercedes-Benz sold negligible EVs while continuing to focus on internal combustion engine vehicles (ICEVs) and hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs, including full hybrids and mild hybrids). These automakers leaned into expanding their hybrid lineups to take advantage of hybrid-specific incentives (though these are tiered below those for EVs). However, in 2026, rising fuel costs and a constrained domestic oil supply likely contributed to greater demand for EVs than for hybrids.

In H1 2026, EVs accounted for 15% of total new LDVs, more than double the 7% in all of 2025. BEVs accounted for 8% of total LDV sales and PHEVs accounted for 7%. HEVs accounted for 8%, with ICEVs making up the remainder (77%).

The Philippines has enacted several measures to support EV uptake. The Electric Vehicle Industry Development Act (EVIDA; Republic Act 11697), signed in April 2022, established the regulatory framework covering EV adoption, charging infrastructure, manufacturing, research and development, and fleet conversion. Building on this law, the Comprehensive Roadmap for the Electric Vehicle Industry (CREVI) laid out a non-binding roadmap with interim targets through 2040. It includes the extension of import tariffs on EVs, HEVs, e-motorcycles, and related components, and the extension of an excise tax for BEVs through 2028. 

On the manufacturing side, President Marcos signed Executive Order 121 on July 29, 2026, establishing the Electric Vehicle Incentive Strategy (EVIS), a fiscal support program capped at ₱60 billion (approximately $954 million). It provides financial support for EV manufacturers through capital incentives of up to 40% of the total capital investment for BEVs (and their components and parts) and 30% for PHEVs and hybrid vehicles (and their component and parts), as well as production incentives of up to 12% of the ex-factory vehicle price. Each registered EV model is eligible for up to ₱15 billion ($239 million) in incentives; manufacturers are required to commit at least ₱5 billion ($80 million) in new investment and launch a locally manufactured EV within 3 years. With the finalization of EVIS, trial production is expected to begin next year and commercial production is targeted before the 2028 elections. 

#### Global production trends

China accounted for roughly two-thirds of total global EV production, a slight decline from the previous year, as other markets, including Vietnam, Türkiye and Thailand, increased manufacturing activity. 

China also accounted for 84% of all EV imports in the emerging markets analyzed in this monitor. They also accounted for 72% of all EV imports into India and 65% of all imports into Europe.
